items.text: Among adults discharged alive after community-acquired pneumonia from the four regional hospitals in 2016 to 2021, what is the hazard of a first cardiovascular event in the first year and in years two to five compared with matched general population controls and with patients admitted for other acute infections, after adjustment for frailty and existing cardiovascular disease?
items.population: Adults discharged alive after community-acquired pneumonia, regional registry, 2016 to 2021
items.comparator: Matched general population adults; adults discharged after urinary tract infection or cellulitis
items.outcome: First myocardial infarction, stroke, heart failure admission or cardiovascular death
items.time: 0 to 1 year and 1 to 5 years after discharge
items.setting: Four hospitals in one region with linked death and admission data

finer: Feasible with existing registry data once linkage is approved; interesting to clinicians and patients; novel beyond 90 days for this region; ethical under the standing approval; relevant to follow-up planning.
summary: One PECO question with two comparison groups and two time windows.
